question.knowledge_point: Finding the Derivative of a Function Given in Implicit Form
question.worked_solution:
First, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ assuming that $y=y(x).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{y}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2y-x) \\ {e}^{y}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}(2y)}{\text{d}x}-\frac{\text{d}(x)}{\text{d}x} \\ {e}^{y}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{y}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-1 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}(2-{e}^{y}) & =1 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2-{e}^{y}}\end{aligned}
$$
